newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes thin, outright prices stumble.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes thin, outright prices stumble.

text.p: U.S. foreign crudes were extremely quiet in light trade Thursday as outright prices stumbled about $1.10 a barrel lower on Iraqi Kurds extending a ceasefire, renewing hope for an Iraqi oil-for-food sale.
Imports continued to prove expensive from the North Sea despite softening European crude premiums, with end-users relaxed in a bearish market, traders said.
Brent was nominally assessed workable, if sold at West Texas Intermediate plus 30 cents cif, but sellers had been seen offering at 15 cents premium, traders said.
The shut arbitrage was also supporting regional sweets.
Cusiana was valued at WTI plus 25 cents fob for November, but availability was deemed thin amid firm demand.
Other regional heavy sweets were also holding at steady levels due to the narrow WTI/Brent arbitrage.
Vasconia for late Nov was priced at better than $2.00 a barrel discount against WTI, and Mendanitos at $1.35 under WTI compared with $1.75 earlier this month.
"The differential between WTI and Brent has been narrow for two months, which has been good for Latin American crudes," a Gulf Coast crude trader said.
Other distressed cargoes on sale included Cabinda, with some traders calling the market at less than $1.00 a barrel discount against WTI, cif U.S. Gulf.
In the U.S. after-market, a U.K. major sold several Dec Brent partials at $22.55 a barrel, down from the London IPE session close of $22.69.
Brent intermonth spreads for Dec/Jan traded at 37 cents, also off from London's 48-44 cents.
